name: Kurt Alme

issue_poll.name: Pew Research Center, U.S. registered voters, Sept 28-Oct 4, 2026 - share calling each issue 'very important' to their 2026 congressional vote; plus University of Montana Crown of the Continent/Greater Yellowstone Initiative poll (New Bridge Strategy/FM3), Montana registered voters (n=515), Mar 19-25, 2026
issue_poll.note: No 2026 Montana poll with a general ranked issue list was found (checked MSU Billings Mountain State Poll Oct 2026, MTFP-Eagleton Jan and May 2026, Gray House June 2026, AARP MT Vital Voices). Fallback: national Pew ranking as the base. One Montana-specific issue was added: public lands, which 71% of Montana voters called an extremely/very serious problem (loss of access to public lands) in the UM poll (https://www.umt.edu/crown-yellowstone/voter-surveys/2026/2026_u_of_montana_deck_d3c.pdf). It was slotted by that share between Pew's 'future of democracy' (73%) and 'healthcare' (68%); the questions differ, so this placement is approximate. Housing and cost of living folded into Economy. That pushed Pew's #10, gun policy (45%), out of the top 10.

issues.detail: Bill withholding congressional pay when Congress misses balanced-budget/budget deadline; signed no-tax-increase pledge; cut housing construction red tape
Work to secure elections; no specific measure
Oppose selling off federal public lands; keep them in public ownership
Oppose taxpayer subsidies to insurers; expand telehealth; require posted prices; back existing Rural Health Transformation Program and Medicaid work requirements
No education position found; did not answer iVoterGuide education questions
Back tighter border security; prosecute or deport dangerous noncitizens using immigration charges; target cartels
Prevent Iranian nuclear weapons; no new ground troops in Iran; oppose limits on weapons use against Iran; use tariffs for fairer Canada trade
Data centers must pay own way, disclose community costs, not raise electricity bills or harm water users
Investigate drug trafficking organizations up to cartels; support law enforcement; public-private partnerships for addiction recovery
No stated position; endorsed by SBA Pro-Life America but made no commitment himself

plan_caveats: Issue ranking is national (Pew) plus one Montana issue (public lands) slotted from a different question in a March UM poll; no Montana-wide ranked issue poll from 2026 was found.

Alme ran a low-detail campaign: skipped the Sept 20 debate, declined most interviews, and left all iVoterGuide questions unanswered; his campaign site (almeforsenate.com) could not be fetched, so site issue pages, if any, were not reviewed.

Economy rated Concrete because of the named congressional pay-withholding bill and signed no-tax-increase pledge (via OnTheIssues summary, https://ontheissues.org/Senate/Kurt_Alme.htm); other economy statements are vague.
Public lands rated Partial: a pledge to oppose sales, not a proposed ban or bill, though votes on land sales can test it.
Immigration detail partly rests on an April 8, 2026 Montana Talks interview (via OnTheIssues) that speaks partly as a prosecutor; border security support is from KPAX primary coverage.
Education rated None; Ballotpedia lists a stance on keeping boys out of girls' sports, which was not treated as an education platform.
Social Security pledge (never cut seniors' benefits, Oct 11 debate) and Second Amendment stance ('defend', vague) fell outside the top 10.
